modules.title: Stress shift and phonetic transcription
modules.html:
Stress shift occurs when the same spelling is stressed on different syllables depending on whether the word is a noun/adjective or a verb.

WordNoun / adj.Verb
record'RE-cordre-'CORD
present'PRE-sentpre-'SENT
object'OB-jectob-'JECT
contract'CON-tractcon-'TRACT
increase'IN-creasein-'CREASE
subject'SUB-jectsub-'JECT
conflict'CON-flictcon-'FLICT

Phonetic transcription

Write words in IPA between slashes: cat /kæt/, night /naɪt/, laughter /ˈlɑːftə/, education /ˌedʒʊˈkeɪʃn/. Learn to identify vowels, consonants, and mark primary (ˈ) and secondary (ˌ) stress.

Key points

  • 'RE-cord'.
  • re-'CORD.

Worked example

Q: Stress in record (noun):
A: 1st syllable

Q: Stress in record (verb):
A: 2nd syllable

modules.title: Rhyme patterns and rhythmic structures
modules.html:
Rhyme is the repetition of the same or similar sounds at the ends of words. In poetry, rhyme schemes are labelled with letters (a, b, c…):

  • Couplet: aa bb.
  • Alternate: abab.
  • Envelope: abba.

Rhythm in speech comes from stressed and unstressed syllables. English is a stress-timed language: stressed syllables occur at roughly equal intervals, and unstressed ones are compressed between them.

In poetry, this becomes metre: a foot such as iambic (u ' u ') or trochaic (' u ' u) repeats a pattern.

Key points

  • 'aa' pair.
  • abab.

Worked example

Q: Rhyme scheme of a couplet:
A: aa

Q: Rhyme scheme of alternate rhyme:
A: abab

examples.q:
Give the rhyme scheme:
'The road was long, / The night was dark, / He sang a song, / And left his mark.'

modules.title: Oral English examination practice
modules.html:
Typical WAEC / NECO Oral English items:

  1. Vowel selection: pick the word with the same vowel as a given word.
  2. Consonant selection: pick the word with the same consonant sound.
  3. Rhyme: pick the word that rhymes with a given word.
  4. Stress: pick where the stress falls (1st, 2nd, 3rd syllable) or the odd word out by stress pattern.
  5. Emphatic stress: given a sentence with a bold word, identify the correct implication.
  6. Function of stress: identify a noun/verb pair.

Practice tips

  • Learn the IPA symbols by heart.
  • Practise minimal pairs: ship/sheep, cat/cut, bit/beat.
  • Read aloud paying attention to stress and intonation.

examples.q: In She 'called him a liar, the emphasis on 'called' implies:
examples.a: That she did not merely think it or say something less — she went as far as to call him a liar.

modules.title: Stress shift in noun/verb pairs
modules.html:
Stress shift in noun/verb pairs is a key part of Oral English (SSS 3, English). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Stress shift occurs when the same spelling is stressed on different syllables depending on whether the word is a noun/adjective or a verb.
  • Verb record 'RE-cord re-'CORD present 'PRE-sent pre-'SENT object 'OB-ject ob-'JECT contract 'CON-tract con-'TRACT increase 'IN-crease in-'CREASE subject 'SUB-ject sub-'JECT conflict 'CON-flict con-'FLICT Phonetic transcription Write words in IPA between slashes: cat /kæt/, night /naɪt/, laughter /ˈlɑːftə/, education /ˌedʒʊˈkeɪʃn/ .
  • Learn to identify vowels, consonants, and mark primary (ˈ) and secondary (ˌ) stress.
  • Worked example Q: Stress in record (noun): A: 1st syllable Q: Stress in record (verb): A: 2nd syllable
  • Rhythm in speech comes from stressed and unstressed syllables.

Worked example

Q: Stress in record (noun):
A: 1st syllable — 'RE-cord'.

Q: Stress in record (verb):
A: 2nd syllable — re-'CORD.

quiz.q: Ade _____ the examination before the results were announced.
quiz.solution: The past perfect 'had written' is used to describe an action completed before another action in the past (the announcement of results).

quiz.q: Identify the word that has a different stress pattern from the others:
quiz.solution: 'Calculate' is stressed on the first syllable (CAL-cu-late), while the others are stressed on the third syllable.

quiz.q: Choose the word with the primary stress on the second syllable:
Identify the word that has a different stress pattern:
quiz.solution: Most two-syllable nouns are stressed on the 1st syllable, while verbs are stressed on the 2nd. 'Refuse' (verb) is re-FUSE, while 'Present' (noun) is PRE-sent.

quiz.q: Choose the word that has a different stress pattern:
quiz.solution: Re-PORT is stressed on the 2nd syllable, while the others are on the 1st.

quiz.q: Emphatic Stress: He DID the work. (The stress implies:)
options: He didn't just talk about it
quiz.solution: Stress on the auxiliary 'did' emphasizes the completion or reality of the action against a doubt.

quiz.q: Which of the following words has the stress on the first syllable?
quiz.solution: 'Calculate' is stressed on the first syllable (CAL-cu-late). Im-POR-tant, de-VE-lop, and ed-u-CA-tion are stressed elsewhere.

quiz.q: Stress pattern: Which word has the primary stress on the third syllable?
quiz.solution: Eco-NO-mic has the stress on the third syllable. TEL-e-vi-sion (1st), pho-TOG-ra-phy (2nd), ad-VEN-ture (2nd).
